files_created.purpose: Library plus command line entry: pure count_text() returning the four integer statistics, main(argv=None, stdin_text=None) returning an int exit code with two separate call scopes (command line writes exactly four stdout lines, programmatic call writes nothing), --encoding limited to file decoding, and one sys.exit(main()) inside the __main__ guard. Docstrings rewritten to cite this round's BC-01..BC-26 only.

Standard library unittest suite (81 tests) mapping every AC-01..AC-25 and BC-01..BC-26 to at least one case: pure function tables, line/non-empty tables, word regex rules, normalisation order, both call scopes, five command line error paths plus their silent programmatic counterparts, --help in both scopes, --encoding, argv semantics, entry point shape, and delivery constraints (no manifests, standard library imports only, README/sample self-consistency, scratch hygiene).

Rewritten documentation: statistics rules keyed to this round's BC numbers, normalisation and line boundary rules, exit-code table, programmatic-call semantics, reproducible examples (sample_input.txt, stdin, immediate EOF, CRLF text via count_text, --encoding with a generated UTF-16LE file, --help, directory error), test instructions, priority list that removes the historical crlf_cr.txt example and the impossible char_count 6 for '  \r\n \r\n', and a boundary condition quick reference BC-01..BC-26.

result.implementation_summary: Delivered examples/text-stats as a standard-library-only tool. count_text(text) normalises in a fixed order (drop one leading U+FEFF, CRLF to LF, remaining CR to LF), then splits on LF only, so line_count and non_empty_line_count come from the same split (empty text has no line, a trailing LF adds no line) and word_count is the count of [A-Za-z]+(?:[-'\u2019][A-Za-z]+)* matches. main() treats stdin_text is None as the command line scope (four 'key: value' stdout lines, exit 0) and any explicit stdin_text, empty string included, as the programmatic scope (no bytes on either stream, never reads sys.stdin, returns 0/1). The five handled errors (missing file, directory or unreadable path, decode failure, unknown --encoding checked with codecs.lookup before input selection, more than one positional argument) return 1 and never argparse's 2; on the command line they print exactly one 'error: ' line and nothing on stdout, while programmatic calls stay completely silent. --help returns 0, verbose for the command line and silent when programmatic. Legacy sources were rewritten rather than patched because their numbering was pervasively stale (a nonexistent BC-27), the README example referenced the absent crlf_cr.txt file, and it still justified the impossible char_count 6; all three delivery sources now cite only AC-01..AC-25 and BC-01..BC-26, and the whitespace CRLF input is consistently 5 / 2 / 0 / 0.
acceptance_criteria_addressed: AC-01 main([], stdin_text="") returns int 0 with empty captured streams and a sys.stdin stub that raises on any read.
AC-02 the documented python -c one-liner exits 0 and prints exactly 'True 0 int'.
AC-03 command line with immediate stdin EOF prints the four zero lines, exit 0, empty stderr, well inside the timeout.
AC-04 count_text returns a dict with exactly the four integer keys (20/2/2/4 for the reference text, 0/0/0/0 for empty) and touches no stream.
AC-05 python text_stats.py sample_input.txt yields 20/2/2/4 with empty stderr.
AC-06 stdin bytes b"hello world\n" yield 12/1/1/2.
AC-07 the PATH route and the stdin byte route agree with count_text on 20/2/2/4.

AC-08 one leading BOM dropped (3 and 4 characters), "a
bc" 5/3/3/3, "  
 
" 5/2/0/0.
AC-09 U+2028, U+2029, \x0b, \x0c, \x1c, \x1d, \x1e, \x85 are not line boundaries (1 line, 3 characters) and the counting code never uses splitlines.
AC-10 the nine-row line_count / non_empty_line_count table matches count_text exactly.
AC-11 the seven-row char_count table matches, including combining marks counting as separate code points.
AC-12 the eighteen-row word_count table matches, including hello--world 2, a1b 2, foo_bar baz 3, it\u2019s 1.
AC-13 stdout is exactly four ordered 'key: value' lines matching the anchored regular expression, no trailing blank line.
AC-14 all five command line error classes exit 1 with empty stdout and one 'error: ' line without traceback.
AC-15 the four programmatic error calls return 1 while writing nothing to either stream.
AC-16 --help exits 0 with usage text mentioning PATH and --encoding on the command line, and is silent in the programmatic scope.
AC-17 main signature has argv=None and stdin_text=None; sys.exit( appears once, inside the __main__ guard; exit codes stay in {0, 1}.
AC-18 main returns only the int 0 while count_text supplies 12/1/1/2.
AC-19 main(["sample_input.txt"], stdin_text="ignored") returns 0 while writing nothing.
AC-20 a UTF-16LE file read with --encoding utf-16-le yields 4/1/1/1.
AC-21 the canonical discovery command runs green (81 tests) and the suite contains explicit programmatic-silence and line-count-table cases.

AC-22 sample_input.txt is exactly 20 LF bytes, the README files and stdin examples match the implementation, no crlf_cr.txt reference survives, no bare U+2019 character appears in module, tests or README.
AC-23 README and tests cite only AC-01..AC-25 and BC-01..BC-26; every criterion number is referenced.
AC-24 the only modified paths are the delivery sources and the injected evidence file, with no dependency manifest and an unchanged __pycache__ listing.
AC-25 both modules import only standard library modules.
